module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1121

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1121](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1121)
- [BeLi16] Bezdek, Károly and Litvak, Alexander E., *Packing convex bodies by cylinders*.
  Discrete Comput. Geom. (2016), 725-738.
- [GoGo45] Goodman, A. W. and Goodman, R. E., *A circle covering theorem*. Amer. Math. Monthly
  (1945), 494-498.
- [Ha47] Hadwiger, H., *Nonseparable convex systems*. Amer. Math. Monthly (1947), 583-585.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos1121

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

/--
If $C_1,\ldots,C_n$ are circles in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with radii $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ such that no line
disjoint from all the circles divides them into two non-empty sets then the circles can be
covered by a circle of radius $r=\sum r_i$.

This is true, and was proved by Goodman and Goodman [GoGo45] (whose proof also generalises to
higher dimensions). A generalisation to convex bodies was proved by Hadwiger [Ha47].

An alternative proof is given by Bezdek and Litvak [BeLi16].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1121.lean"]
theorem erdos_1121 {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → ℝ²) (r : Fin n → ℝ) (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i)
    (hsep : ∀ (v : ℝ²) (t : ℝ), v ≠ 0 →
      (∀ i, ∀ p ∈ Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i), inner ℝ v p ≠ t) →
      (∀ i, inner ℝ v (c i) < t) ∨ (∀ i, t < inner ℝ v (c i))) :
    ∃ z : ℝ², (⋃ i, Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i)) ⊆ Metric.closedBall z (∑ i, r i) := by
  sorry

/--
The proof of Goodman and Goodman [GoGo45] also generalises to higher dimensions: if
$B_1,\ldots,B_n$ are balls in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with radii $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ such that no hyperplane
disjoint from all the balls divides them into two non-empty sets then the balls can be covered by
a ball of radius $r=\sum r_i$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_1121.variants.higher_dimension {d n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (r : Fin n → ℝ) (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i)
    (hsep : ∀ (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (t : ℝ), v ≠ 0 →
      (∀ i, ∀ p ∈ Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i), inner ℝ v p ≠ t) →
      (∀ i, inner ℝ v (c i) < t) ∨ (∀ i, t < inner ℝ v (c i))) :
    ∃ z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
      (⋃ i, Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i)) ⊆ Metric.closedBall z (∑ i, r i) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1121

reformulations.difference: For a line avoiding every disk, hsep requires all centers to lie strictly on the same side, rather than explicitly requiring the whole disks to lie on that side.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Positive radii ensure that centers belong to their disks. Each disk is convex, so if one of its points were across an avoiding line from its center, the segment between them would intersect the line. Thus the center and every point of the disk have the same strict side. The all-centers disjunction is therefore equivalent to the all-points disjunction and to the absence of two nonempty sides. Both equivalences were checked in scratch.lean as hsep_iff_full_balls and hsep_iff_no_two_centers. Nonzero normals and real offsets represent all affine lines.

reformulations.difference: The nonseparability hypothesis uses strict half-space inequalities for the centers instead of explicitly stating that an avoiding hyperplane cannot separate the balls into two nonempty subfamilies.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The same convexity and center-membership argument works in every dimension: a ball disjoint from a hyperplane lies wholly on the side containing its center. The dimension-polymorphic Lean proofs hsep_iff_full_balls and hsep_iff_no_two_centers establish the relevant equivalences. Every affine hyperplane in Euclidean space has the stated nonzero-normal/offset representation.

sources_consulted: Goodman, A. W. and Goodman, R. E., “A circle covering theorem,” American Mathematical Monthly 52 (1945), 494–498, especially Theorem 1, the closed-set convention on p. 494, and the higher-dimensional remark. Archival text: https://archive.org/download/sim_american-mathematical-monthly_1945-10_52_8/sim_american-mathematical-monthly_1945-10_52_8_djvu.txt (the archive item also contains the November article).

Hadwiger, H., “Nonseparable convex systems,” American Mathematical Monthly 54 (1947), 583–585. Archival text: https://archive.org/download/sim_american-mathematical-monthly_1947-12_54_10/sim_american-mathematical-monthly_1947-12_54_10_djvu.txt

Bezdek, K. and Litvak, A. E., “Packing convex bodies by cylinders,” arXiv:1507.05115v2, §6, especially the definition of nonseparability and Theorem 6.1. LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1507.05115v2
Bezdek, K. and Lángi, Z., “On non-separable families of positive homothetic convex bodies,” arXiv:1602.01020v3, introduction and §4. LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1602.01020v3

review.notes: Both declarations faithfully state the cited results. Checked the Euclidean metric, closed-ball semantics, quantifiers, strict separation bounds, positive-radius hypotheses, and exact radius sum. Lean checks passed for n = 0, n = 1, and d = 0; common-point families satisfy hsep, so it is not an impossible hypothesis. The linked formal proof was checked in /workspace/review with a namespace rename and one compatibility change from `convert` to `convert!` for Lean 4.33.1. Its main theorem and a bridge to the exact repository statement have only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound as axioms. Direct access to erdosproblems.com was blocked by Cloudflare despite descriptive User-Agent headers; the original cited papers supplied the mathematical source, and the independent problem database corroborates the proved/Lean status.
